_meta.description: Document-rules config for sale_deed — Sale deed for immovable property under Transfer of Property Act 1882 S.54-55. Mandatory registration under Registration Act 1908 S.17 for property > Rs.100. Cites Suraj Lamp v. State of Haryana (2012) 1 SCC 656 — GPA-cum-Sale is NOT a valid transfer of title.
_meta.change_protocol: All edits require CLO sign-off. Stamp duty schedules vary by state — list state-wise references but do NOT hardcode rates. Suraj Lamp disclaimer mandatory when user proposes GPA-cum-sale shortcut.

title: Sale Deed (Transfer of Property Act, 1882 — S.54-55)

causeTitle.format:
SALE DEED

This Sale Deed is executed on this {date} at {place}.

BETWEEN

{vendor_name}, son/daughter/wife of {vendor_father_name}, aged about {vendor_age} years, resident of {vendor_address}, (PAN: {vendor_pan}, Aadhaar last 4: {vendor_aadhaar_last4})
(hereinafter referred to as the "VENDOR" / "SELLER", which expression shall, unless repugnant to the context, include his/her legal heirs, executors, administrators and assigns) of the ONE PART

AND

{purchaser_name}, son/daughter/wife of {purchaser_father_name}, aged about {purchaser_age} years, resident of {purchaser_address}, (PAN: {purchaser_pan}, Aadhaar last 4: {purchaser_aadhaar_last4})
(hereinafter referred to as the "PURCHASER" / "BUYER", which expression shall, unless repugnant to the context, include his/her legal heirs, executors, administrators and assigns) of the OTHER PART.

promptInstructions: Draft a SALE DEED for ABSOLUTE conveyance of immovable property under Transfer of Property Act, 1882, Sections 54 (Sale defined) and 55 (Rights and liabilities of buyer and seller).

CRITICAL — Section 54 TPA: 'Sale' = transfer of ownership in exchange for a price paid or promised. For tangible immovable property of value Rs.100 or upwards, sale can be made ONLY by a registered instrument.

CRITICAL — Section 17(1)(b) Registration Act, 1908: Non-testamentary instruments which purport or operate to create, declare, assign, limit or extinguish any right, title or interest of value of Rs.100 and upwards, to or in immovable property, MUST be registered. UNREGISTERED SALE DEED DOES NOT TRANSFER TITLE.

CRITICAL — Suraj Lamp & Industries Pvt Ltd v. State of Haryana (2012) 1 SCC 656: 'GPA-cum-Sale' or 'SA-cum-GPA-cum-Will' transactions are NOT valid modes of transfer of immovable property. Title can pass ONLY by registered sale deed. ALWAYS WARN the advocate if any GPA-cum-sale shortcut is being attempted — explicitly flag it in the draft cover note.

Start with RECITAL OF TITLE: trace the vendor's title — prior sale deed number, date, registration details; or inheritance with succession certificate / mutation; or partition deed; or settlement deed. Include mutation entry numbers in revenue records (Bihar — Jamabandi; UP — Khatauni; Jharkhand — Khatian; Delhi — Mutation Register).

PROPERTY DESCRIPTION (Schedule A) must include: (a) Full postal address, (b) Khasra / Survey / Plot No., (c) Khata / Patta No., (d) Total extent (area in sq ft / sq m for plots and houses; acres + decimals for agricultural land), (e) Boundaries — North, South, East, West with neighbour's name/property/feature, (f) Registration Sub-District + Tehsil + District.

CONSIDERATION: state amount in figures AND words. State mode of payment — cash (NOTE: cash above Rs.20,000 attracts Income Tax Act S.269SS / 269T penalties; advise bank transfer / DD / RTGS), cheque (with number, date, bank), DD, RTGS / NEFT (with UTR). Receipt clause must explicitly acknowledge full receipt; if part payment, state schedule.

OPERATIVE TRANSFER CLAUSE: 'The Vendor doth hereby grant, convey, transfer, sell, assign and assure unto the Purchaser, his heirs, executors, administrators and assigns ABSOLUTELY AND FOREVER, ALL THAT piece and parcel of land/property more fully described in the Schedule A hereunder written, together with all rights, easements, privileges, appurtenances, structures, walls, fences, trees, water, water-courses, lights, liberties and advantages whatsoever appertaining thereto...'
DELIVERY OF POSSESSION clause: state date of physical delivery; if vacant possession or subject to existing tenant — specify.

VENDOR'S WARRANTIES under S.55(2) TPA — vendor shall be deemed to contract with buyer that the interest which the seller professes to transfer to the buyer subsists and that he has power to transfer the same. Include explicit warranties of: (a) absolute marketable title; (b) free from encumbrances, mortgages, charges, liens, attachments, court orders; (c) no pending litigation; (d) all statutory dues paid; (e) no acquisition / requisition notices; (f) urban land ceiling NOC if applicable; (g) agricultural ceiling compliance if agricultural land.
ENCUMBRANCES DECLARATION: vendor declares property is free from all encumbrances. If any subsisting mortgage being redeemed from sale proceeds — set out mechanism.

AGRICULTURAL LAND CAVEATS: state-specific restrictions on agricultural land transfer:
   - Bihar: Bihar Tenancy Act, 1885 — restrictions on transfer of raiyati holdings; SC/ST Land Transfer Regulation (CNT / SPT Act in adjoining Jharkhand applies in some Bihar tribal areas).
   - Jharkhand: Chotanagpur Tenancy Act, 1908 (CNT Act) — bars transfer of tribal/ST land except with permission of Deputy Commissioner. Santhal Parganas Tenancy Act, 1949 (SPT Act) — even more restrictive for Santhal Pargana.
   - UP: UP Zamindari Abolition & Land Reforms Act, 1950; UP Revenue Code, 2006 — restrictions on transfer of agricultural land; ceiling under UP Imposition of Ceiling on Land Holdings Act, 1960.
   - Delhi: Delhi Land Reforms Act, 1954 — bhumidhar / asami restrictions.
INDEMNITY CLAUSE: vendor indemnifies and holds harmless the purchaser against any loss, damage, expense arising from defect in title, prior charges, or breach of any covenant.

STAMP DUTY: state amount paid and on which the deed is engrossed. State-specific:
   - Bihar: ~6% (male) / 5.7% (female) of consideration or circle rate (whichever higher) + 2% registration fee.
   - Jharkhand: ~4% (male) / 3% (female) + 3% registration fee.
   - UP: 7% (male) / 6% (female where 1% rebate) + 1% registration fee.
   - Delhi: 6% (male) / 4% (female) + 1% registration fee.
   NOTE — DO NOT hardcode rates; user must verify current rates with state's stamp duty calculator / Sub-Registrar. State 'rates current as of advocate's verification at time of execution'.

Where consideration < Circle Rate / Collector Rate — Income Tax Act S.50C / 56(2)(x) consequences: difference treated as deemed consideration for capital gains and as income from other sources for purchaser. Advise client to consult CA.
MUTATION clause: vendor authorises purchaser to apply for mutation; vendor agrees to cooperate.
Standard registration endorsement space at end.

TWO WITNESSES — full names, parentage, addresses, signatures. (Registration Act + state rules typically require two adult witnesses; for SR registration, the parties must appear personally with photographs and Aadhaar / ID.)
Where vendor / purchaser is a HUF — Karta executes; mention HUF status and that property is sold in capacity of Karta with consent of all adult coparceners.
Where vendor / purchaser is a company — board resolution annexed; signed by authorised signatory.
Where minor coparcener interest exists — court permission under Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 OR Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 required; flag this prominently.

Where property is ancestral coparcenary — daughters' coparcenary rights post HSA 2005 amendment (Vineeta Sharma v. Rakesh Sharma 2020 — daughters are coparceners by birth even if father died before 2005); advise all coparceners must be parties or grant NOC.

Append Lawie disclaimer: 'This sale deed is a drafting assistant output. The executing advocate is responsible for legal accuracy, due diligence on title, stamp duty correctness, registration formalities, and statutory compliance. Lawie is not legal counsel to either party.'

sections.description: Sale defined; mode of transfer; agreement to sell does not by itself create interest
Rights and liabilities of buyer and seller (warranties, indemnities)
Persons competent to transfer
Conditions restraining alienation void
Transfer for benefit of unborn person
Documents of which registration is compulsory — includes sale deed of immovable property of value Rs.100+
Time for presentation — within 4 months of execution
Persons to present documents for registration
Effect of non-registration — unregistered sale deed does not affect property nor be received as evidence
Instruments chargeable with duty
Instruments executed in India to be stamped before or at execution
Unstamped / insufficiently stamped instruments inadmissible in evidence
Conveyance / Sale stamp rates — state-specific
Stamp duty value as deemed consideration for capital gains where consideration < SDV
Where purchaser receives property for less than SDV, difference taxed as income from other sources
TDS at 1% on consideration where property value >= Rs.50 lakh
Bar on cash transactions above Rs.20,000 in immovable property dealings
Restrictions on raiyati land transfer in Bihar
Tribal / ST land transfer restrictions in Jharkhand
Santhal Pargana restrictions
UP agricultural land regime
Bhumidhar / asami in Delhi rural
Daughters as coparceners (post 2005 amendment, Vineeta Sharma)
Mandatory RERA registration of projects > 500 sqm or 8 units — sale by developer must be of RERA-registered project
No deposit / advance > 10% before agreement for sale
Adherence to sanctioned plans

filing_checklist: Draft engrossed on Non-Judicial Stamp Paper of correct value (state-specific schedule)
Stamp duty calculated on whichever is HIGHER of (a) consideration or (b) Circle Rate / Collector Rate / Stamp Duty Value
Original title documents of vendor available for inspection by Sub-Registrar
Encumbrance Certificate (EC) for past 13/30 years from Sub-Registrar's office
Mutation entries / Jamabandi / Khatauni / Khatian extract — current
Property tax receipts up to date (vendor to clear arrears)
Society / RWA NOC if apartment / cooperative society
RERA registration certificate (if project under RERA)
Approved sanction plan / occupancy certificate (for built-up structures)
PAN of both parties (mandatory)
Aadhaar of both parties (mandatory for SR registration)
Passport-size photographs of both parties (2 each, recent)
Form 60 if PAN not available (rare)
TDS Form 26QB filed by purchaser if value >= Rs.50 lakh (1% TDS u/s 194-IA)
Two adult witnesses with own ID proofs and addresses present at SR office
Both parties physically present at Sub-Registrar office for execution & registration
Biometric / iris scan as required by SR office (Aadhaar-linked verification)
Online slot booking on state SR portal where applicable (UP — IGRSUP; Delhi — DORIS; Bihar — Bhumijankari; Jharkhand — JharBhoomi)
Registration within 4 months of execution date (S.23 Registration Act) — penalty for delay up to 10x stamp duty
After registration — apply for mutation in revenue / municipal records
Notify society / association / electricity / water utilities for name change
Update property tax record in purchaser's name
Where agricultural land in Jharkhand tribal area — Deputy Commissioner's permission under CNT/SPT Act ANNEXED
Where minor's interest involved — court permission order ANNEXED
Where company is party — Board Resolution + Memorandum of Association ANNEXED
Lawie disclaimer prominently included
validation_rules: stamp_duty_paid must be > 0 — flag if appears below state's minimum schedule
if consideration_amount < circle_rate_or_collector_rate — display Section 50C / 56(2)(x) IT Act warning
if consideration_amount >= 5000000 (Rs.50 lakh) — flag mandatory TDS u/s 194-IA
if property_type == 'agricultural_land' and state == 'jharkhand' — flag CNT / SPT Act permission requirement
if property_type == 'agricultural_land' and state == 'bihar' — flag Bihar Tenancy Act restrictions
property_boundaries must contain mention of all four directions (N/S/E/W)
encumbrances field must explicitly state 'NIL' or list encumbrances — never blank
vendor_pan and purchaser_pan must be 10 alphanumeric characters
witness_1_name_address and witness_2_name_address are both mandatory
advocate must include Bar Council enrollment number
